dedupe_keys.name: dsdpm 66 open image dataset for intelligent monitoring of underground drilling operations in coal mines

description: DsDPM 66 is a benchmark image dataset for computer vision at coal mine heading faces: 105,096 images taken from videos of 66 underground drilling operation scenes, annotated by hand for object detection and pose estimation. The figshare records say it was benchmarked with models such as YOLOv8 and DETR, and that because of storage limits it is split across two items: one with the drill rig, drill pipe and miner-and-drill-pipe interaction categories (zip files of about 5.4, 9.6 and 4.8 GB) and one with coal miner, compressed oxygen self-rescuer and mining helmet categories (about 5.4, 6.9 and 4.6 GB). Both were published on 14 March 2025 (version 2) under CC BY 4.0; a third item of 13 May 2025 links the dataset to its Scientific Data article. Coverage is coal mine heading faces; the mines and their country are not stated on the pages read. Caveats: the data suit safety monitoring algorithms, not system simulation, and the files are large. For simulation it gives labelled data for automated monitoring of worker safety and equipment at the face, which feeds operational risk and incident models for underground mining. A related catalogue record is the China mine accident report dataset.
